import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data

# Calculate average spending for each category

plt.xlabel('Category')
plt.ylabel('Average Spending')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

import pandas as pd
import numpy as np
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the data
customer_segments = pd.read_csv('data/customer_segments.csv')

# Calculate average spending for each category
avg_spending = customer_segments[['MntWines', 'MntFruits', 'MntMeatProducts', 'MntFishProducts', 'MntSweetProducts', 'MntGoldProds']].mean()

# Create a bar plot to visualize the average spending for each category
plt.figure(figsize=(10,6))
sns.barplot(x=avg_spending.index, y=avg_spending.values)
plt.title('Average Spending by Category')
plt.xlabel('Category')
plt.ylabel('Average Spending')
plt.xticks(rotation=45)
plt.tight_layout()

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)
